01 / The research stack

Four decisions. One reproducible lab.

The project combines established optimization techniques with empirical forecast calibration and explicit reference formulations. It proposes an integrated experimental workflow; it does not claim a new theorem or priority over the literature.

01 / DISPATCH

Price the tail risk.

Co-optimize energy and upward reserves using expected exceedance and CVaR. Evaluate on the following seven days.

02 / COMMITMENT

Schedule the fleet.

A thermal MILP with startup costs, minimum on/off times, ramps and reserves calibrated from prior forecast errors.

03 / NETWORK

Add limits as needed.

DC-OPF constraint generation adds violated thermal limits, then validates all branches against a full formulation.

04 / EXPANSION

Separate build and operate.

Multicut Benders chooses continuous generation capacity under seasonal and demand-growth scenarios.

02 / Evidence, with limits

What the models actually found.

RTS-GMLC is a synthetic test system geographically assigned to the U.S. Southwest. Its load and renewable series model 2020. It is not a record of an actual utility's dispatch. Costs combine upstream fuel assumptions and 2024 EIA construction observations; scenario parameters are disclosed separately.

Interpretation

CVaR dispatch reduced the sum of mean daily held-out reserve exceedances by 98.3% relative to zero-reserve dispatch across the included seasonal cases (13,581.4 to 236.7 MWh). Reserve procurement costs increased by $496,407 over the modeled operating days. Risk-neutral procurement produced 2,142.3 MWh on the same aggregate exceedance measure. On the common $50/MWh exceedance-price metric, CVaR's summed held-out proxy cost was $4,033,160, versus $3,870,274 for risk-neutral procurement. The lower tail risk therefore has a visible procurement-cost tradeoff in this run. These exceedances are a procurement-risk proxy; they are not measured blackouts.

All screened DC-OPF objectives matched their full-limit counterparts within the experiment tolerance. Screened solves retained 0–5 of 120 line-limit pairs, and every final flow was checked against every rating. Constraint reduction alone does not establish a runtime advantage.

UC schedules had a maximum reported relative MIP gap of 1.148%. 5 solves returned a validated incumbent at the time limit. Small cost differences between reserve policies should be interpreted alongside their solver bounds.

At the assumed $75/t carbon price, planning built 0.0 MW solar, 0.0 MW wind and 2,864.6 MW gas, at an illustrative annual objective of $1.851 billion. Benders and extensive LP objectives agreed for every tested carbon price. The base result can favor gas because existing low-cost generation supplies much of the sampled energy and new capacity covers residual peaks. At $150/t, the build changed to 1,624.1 MW solar, 1,452.6 MW wind and 2,857.4 MW gas. Mean observed planning runtime was 2.48s for Benders and 0.26s for the extensive LP; decomposition was slower on this small benchmark. Four hand-selected days, simplified retirements, and mixed-vintage cost assumptions limit any investment interpretation.

How to read the evidence

ED exceedance is the amount by which a forecast error exceeds a purchased upward-reserve quantity. The experiment does not simulate reserve deployment or claim an outage probability.

UC reports a solver bound and actual relative MIP gap. OPF is lossless DC and excludes voltage, reactive power, contingencies and dynamic security.

Planning uses 12 scenarios: four fixed seasonal days crossed with three growth levels. Equal day weights sum to 8,760 annual hours. This demonstrates decomposition rather than a validated investment forecast.

03 / Start here

Run it. Inspect it. Extend it.

The compact benchmark is included. No API key, commercial solver or data download is required for the experiments.

git clone https://github.com/BehnamMohseniGharyehsafa/gridopt-lab.git
cd gridopt-lab
python -m venv .venv
# Activate .venv for your operating system (see README).
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
gridopt validate
python -m pytest -q
gridopt run --output results/runs/my-run
gridopt report --input results/runs/my-run
